title: A Street Silk Road Traders Settled 1,200 Years Ago | China Travel Expert
description:
Silk Road merchants settled this Xi’an street over 1,200 years ago — and it never stopped humming.

From the Tang dynasty, Arab and Persian Muslim traders followed the Silk Road to Chang’an — today’s Xi’an — and settled around what is now the Muslim Quarter. Tucked in its lanes is the Great Mosque of Huajue Lane, founded in 742: one of China’s four great mosques, and the best-preserved mosque built entirely in traditional Chinese style — courtyards, timber halls and an east-west axis instead of domes. Huajue Lane itself is one of the best-kept Ming-Qing lanes in the quarter.

🧭 Expert Tip: Skip the packed food strip at night — walk Huajue Lane to the Great Mosque early, before the crowds.

一条街，商队住了一千二百年；巷子深处，一座长得像庙宇的清真寺。
